summary: Service portal login fails after auth-algorithm rollout — Okta SSO assertion signature mismatch
description:
Issue summary:
After yesterday's cryptographic algorithm rollout on the auth stack (migration from RS256 to RS512 signatures at the edge), a subset of internal users report being unable to sign into the service portal. The Okta SSO flow completes at the IdP side, but the portal returns a 401 and logs show an 'assertion signature invalid' error from the edge verification service.

Impact:
- ~6 internal employees are unable to access the service portal and internal dashboards (eng, oncall).
- Affects both console web UI and API calls that rely on SSO session exchange.
- No customer-facing systems appear affected.

Timeline:
- 2026-03-13 22:00 UTC: Auth algorithm rollout completed (edge-proxy + verifier) per runbook.
- 2026-03-14 08:12 UTC: First report from oncall that service portal login fails.
- 2026-03-14 08:25 UTC: Support ticket opened (this issue).

Steps to reproduce:
1. Attempt Okta SSO login to service portal (https://portal.internal.redwood.com) with an affected user account.
2. Okta challenge completes and IdP redirects back to portal with SAML/OIDC response.
3. Edge-proxy validates assertion, returns 401 with 'invalid signature' in logs.

Observed logs (edge-proxy verifier):
- verifier: signature_verify_error: expected alg=RS512, got alg=RS256, token_kid=auth-legacy-kid-33
- verifier: rejecting assertion for sub=user@company.com; reason=signature_mismatch

Hypothesis & initial findings:
- The rollout changed accepted signing algorithms to prefer RS512; some older Okta app integrations (legacy service accounts / JIT clients) are still issuing RS256-signed assertions. The verifier now rejects those tokens.
- A small percentage of users (6 reported) are using older service tokens stored in password managers or browser sessions that re-use legacy keys.
- The change should have allowed RS256 as fallback per rollout plan, but the edge-proxy's algorithm negotiation may have been misconfigured in the newly deployed image.

Immediate impact mitigation suggestion:
- Roll back verifier config to allow RS256 temporarily, or deploy a hotfix to the verifier to accept both RS256 and RS512 for existing Okta app KIDs.
- Alternatively, identify affected KIDs in Okta and trigger key-rotation for legacy apps (less immediate).

Attachments / evidence:
- Excerpted logs from edge-proxy (see related_confluence_pages).
- Affected user list (internal): liam.chen@redwood.com, marie.kapoor@redwood.com, samir.khan@redwood.com (redacted in this ticket).
comments: 2026-03-14 08:30 - Diego Marquez (SRE): Confirmed signature_mismatch in verifier logs. Adding auth and edge-proxy teams. Marking as Sev1 due to oncall impact.

2026-03-14 08:42 - Priya Nambiar (Auth Eng): I saw the same errors in staging during algorithm QA but assumed fallback was in place. Investigating deployment config: edge-proxy image 1.12.0 explicit alg list may have been set to 'RS512' only.
2026-03-14 09:05 - Aisha Patel (Support): Affected users report that re-logging into Okta via incognito or clearing saved sessions sometimes works — suggests cached legacy tokens in browser sessions.

2026-03-14 09:20 - Diego Marquez (SRE): Temporary mitigation: toggled verifier to accept RS256+RS512 on canary cluster (us-east-canary). Need approval to roll to prod; risk assessment attached in comments.
2026-03-14 10:10 - Priya Nambiar (Auth Eng): Patch PR opened to restore fallback: github.com/redwood-inference/auth-service/pull/1245. Requesting rollback window or expedited rollout.
2026-03-14 11:00 - Diego Marquez (SRE): Approved canary rollout for 30 min. Notifying oncall and #incidents channel. Will monitor for errors and user reports.
investigation_notes: Okta app 'internal-service-portal' still signs several assertions with RS256 using KID auth-legacy-kid-33.
No evidence of key compromise; this is a compatibility gap introduced by a stricter verifier setting during rollout.
Affected users are mostly on older corporate-managed laptops with long-lived Okta sessions; clearing session forces fresh RS512-signed assertion.
Reproducible on us-east and eu-west when using older KID and browser session; not reproducible when acquiring a fresh assertion.
next_steps: Promote PR github.com/redwood-inference/auth-service/pull/1245 to prod to restore RS256 fallback (Auth Eng).
Coordinate 15-minute maintenance window for verifier config change and monitor error rates (SRE).
Notify affected users with instructions to clear Okta sessions as interim workaround (Support).
Audit Okta apps for legacy KIDs and schedule key-rotation / deprecation plan (Security/Auth team).
Create postmortem entry after resolution documenting rollout test gaps and add a regression test to CI.
